author: Good Enough
description:
In the late 1800s and early 1900s, one of the most famous performers in traveling circuses and sideshows was the Bearded Lady. Women with a rare condition called hirsutism, which causes excessive hair growth, often performed in “freak shows,” where audiences were fascinated by unusual human traits.

One of the most well known examples was Annie Jones, who became a star attraction in the circus world and performed for decades. While many performers were initially exploited, some eventually gained financial independence and even pushed back against the term “freak show.”

The Bearded Lady became one of the most iconic figures in circus history.
